passage: Helping to match people with jobs is an essential part of the role played by EURES – the European employment service, which brings together job services across the EU. It provides information, advice and help in finding a job in 27 EU countries, plus Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Switzerland. EURES also has a network of more than 850 specialised advisers who can offer personalised help and advice on the practical, legal and administrative aspects of moving between countries. The proof of the success of EURES lies in the statistics: more and more employers and employees are using the service. In the past three years, the number of vacancies on the EURES portal has grown by 18%, the number of employee CVs by 12%, and - most importantly - the number of employers by 129%. Every month 700,000 people visit the EURES portal, making it one of the busiest EU internet sites.
question: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Most EU internet sites attract more than 700,000 visits per month.
The number of vacancies advertised on the EURES portal has increased by 6% each year.
Historically there has been no way of matching European jobs with candidates throughout the region.
There is a viable international employment marketplace within Europe.

Different skillsets are required for researchers to succeed in academia or business.

Fewer than half mobile EU citizen could be called economically active.

Detalle por opcion:

The passage says that “Such contracts are not bad in themselves: they allow firms to test workers before offering an open-ended contract, and they also allow young people to try out one or more jobs over their first years in the labour market.” These benefits to both young people and businesses can be viewed as a win-win situation.

passage: Young people often face job insecurity and can become trapped in a series of temporary contracts. At present 40% of employees in the EU under 25 years old are on temporary contracts. Such contracts are not bad in themselves: they allow firms to test workers before offering an open-ended contract, and they also allow young people to try out one or more jobs over their first years in the labour market. But too many young people get stuck in a series of temporary jobs, especially in countries where permanent jobs are strongly protected by employment legislation. This results in a two-tier labour market where young workers have little chance of moving to more stable, open-ended contracts. The Commission therefore recommends that Member States with such employment rules introduce an open-ended "single" contract with a gradual increase in employee protection rights, to make it more attractive for employers to hire young people.
question: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: The number of young people on a temporary contract is proportionally higher than older age groups.
Temporary contracts can present a win-win situation for young people and businesses.
The employment status of workers in their first roles can have a profound life-long impact.
The inexperience of young people makes them more risky to employ than older workers.

passage: Consumers still cannot take full advantage of competitive prices and a wide range of choice available in a European Digital Single Market. options: US websites are perceived as safer and more credible within Europe than those based within the EU.
Fragmentation within in the European digital market leads to missed economic opportunities.
More illegal music downloads take place within the European Union than in the United States.

passage: In the past, men and women sometimes paid a different price for different types of insurance because of their sex. Those customers who previously paid less (such as young women for car insurance) will likely see rises in their insurance premiums. But by the same measure, those who paid more (such as men for term-life insurance), are likely to pay less in future. Overall, the changes should balance out over time, but the actual impact of the changes is hard to predict. options: Prices are likely to rise for all customers in the short-term as insurers pass on costs from updating their pricing systems.
The prices that insurers offer are dependent upon their current customer base as well as the individual customer.

Detalle por opcion:

- **A.** Incorrect. There is no evidence within the passage about the likely impact of the policy change on prices.
- **B.** Incorrect. The passage recognises situations in which people can be treated differently e.g. driving behaviour, but makes clear that people cannot be treated differently because of their gender.

The passage makes it clear that gender cannot be the basis for price differences. “From 21 December 2012, insurance companies in the European Union will have to charge the same price to men and women for the same insurance products, without distinction on the grounds of sex” and ”This ‘unisex’ or gender-neutral pricing means men and women with the same characteristics (e.g. age, state of health depending on the product) should pay the same price for the same product.”

passage: From 21 December 2012, insurance companies in the European Union will have to charge the same price to men and women for the same insurance products, without distinction on the grounds of sex. The change will apply to all new contracts for insurance products, including car insurance, life insurance and annuities. This ‘unisex’ or gender-neutral pricing means men and women with the same characteristics (e.g. age, state of health depending on the product) should pay the same price for the same product. Pricing will have to be based on other risk factors than sex, such as driving behaviour in the case of car insurance. This means people will no longer have to pay more, or less, simply because of their gender.
question: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Implementing the ‘unisex’ pricing policy means that prices will rise for most customers.
Equality means treating everyone the same regardless of their personal characteristics.
It is appropriate to charge different insurance prices to men and women when there is a proven gender related risk factor.
Unisex pricing challenges the insurance industry to develop new risk assessment models.

If no volunteers are willing to give up their reservations airlines allocate seats on a first-come first-served basis.
The process of managing an overbooking situation is governed by a legally binding set of rules.
